summary: A person may pick up his child even if the child is holding a muktzeh stone. Terumah that became tamei may be moved together with good food.

chunks.he: נוֹטֵל אָדָם אֶת בְּנוֹ וְהָאֶבֶן בְּיָדוֹ,
chunks.en: A person may pick up his son with a stone in his hand,
chunks.st: A person may take his son in his hands on Shabbat, and even though there is a stone, which is a set-aside item, in the child’s hand, it is not prohibited to pick up the child.

chunks.en: and a basket with a stone in it.
chunks.st: And it is permissible to take a basket with a stone inside it on Shabbat.

chunks.en: And we may move terumah that is tamei together with
chunks.st: And one may move ritually impure teruma, which may not be eaten and is set-aside,

chunks.en: terumah that is tahor and with chullin.
chunks.st: with ritually pure teruma, as well as with non-sacred produce.

words.note: Regular food that is not holy.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.he: אַף מַעֲלִין אֶת הַמְדֻמָּע בְּאֶחָד וּמֵאָה:
chunks.en: we may even lift out the terumah from a mix of one in a hundred.
chunks.explain: Terumah mixed into a hundred times as much regular food.
chunks.st: One may even lift a measure of teruma that was nullified from a mixture of one hundred measures of non-sacred produce and one
chunks.stMore: measure of teruma. When a measure of teruma is mixed with non-sacred produce, if the non-sacred produce is one hundred times the measure of teruma, the teruma is nullified. However, the Sages instituted that one must remove an amount equivalent to that measure of teruma and give it to a priest. The remainder is considered non-sacred produce. Rabbi Yehuda permits removing that measure on Shabbat to render the mixture permitted to eat.

summary: We may not lift a muktzeh thing on Shabbos, but we may tip or shake what it is on so it falls off. The mishnah also teaches how to clean a dirty pillow.

chunks.en: A stone that is on the mouth of a barrel:
chunks.st: a stone, which is set-aside on Shabbat and may not be moved, that was placed on the mouth of a barrel,

chunks.en: he tips the barrel on its side and it falls.
chunks.st: one tilts the barrel on its side, and the stone falls.

chunks.en: If it was between other barrels,
chunks.st: If the barrel was among other barrels,
chunks.stMore: and the other barrels might break if the stone falls on them,

chunks.he: מַגְבִּיהַּ וּמַטָּהּ עַל צִדָּהּ וְהִיא נוֹפֶלֶת.
chunks.en: he lifts it, tips it on its side, and it falls.
chunks.st: he lifts the barrel to distance it from the other barrels, and then tilts it on its side, and the stone falls. With regard to

chunks.en: Coins that are on a pillow:
chunks.st: coins that are on a cushion,

chunks.en: he shakes the pillow and they fall.
chunks.st: he shakes the cushion and the coins fall.

chunks.en: If there was bird mess on it,
chunks.st: If there was bird dung (Arukh) on the cushion,

chunks.en: he wipes it with a rag.
chunks.st: he wipes it with a rag,
chunks.stMore: but he may not wash it with water because of the prohibition against laundering. If the cushion

chunks.en: If it was made of leather,
chunks.st: was made of leather, and laundering is not a concern,

chunks.en: we pour water on it until it is gone.
chunks.st: he places water on it until the bird dung ceases.

summary: Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue about how to clear bones and shells from the table on Shabbos. The mishnah also teaches about using a sponge on Shabbos.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: we may lift bones and shells off the table.
chunks.st: One may clear bones and shells left from the Shabbat meal from the table with his hand.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: he takes the whole tabletop and shakes it off.
chunks.st: One may remove the entire board [tavla] that is the table surface and shake the bones and shells off of it,
chunks.stMore: but he may not lift them with his hand because they are set-aside and may not be moved.

chunks.he: מַעֲבִירִין מִלִּפְנֵי הַשֻּׁלְחָן פֵּרוּרִין פָּחוֹת מִכַּזַּיִת
chunks.en: We may clear crumbs smaller than an olive's size from the table,
chunks.st: One may clear bread crumbs from the table, even if they are less than an olive-bulk,

chunks.he: וְשֵׂעָר שֶׁל אֲפוּנִין וְשֵׂעָר שֶׁל עֲדָשִׁים,
chunks.en: and pea pods and lentil pods,
chunks.st: and pea and lentil pods.
chunks.stMore: Even though it is not fit for human consumption, it may be moved

chunks.en: because they are animal food.
chunks.st: because it is animal fodder. With regard to

chunks.he: סְפוֹג, אִם יֶשׁ לוֹ עוֹר בֵּית אֲחִיזָה,
chunks.en: A sponge: if it has a leather handle,
chunks.st: a sponge, if it has leather as a handle,

chunks.en: we may wipe with it,
chunks.st: one may wipe the table with it,

chunks.en: and if not,
chunks.st: and if not,

chunks.en: we may not wipe with it.
chunks.st: one may not wipe the table with it lest he come to squeeze liquid from it.

chunks.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ,
chunks.en: And the Sages say, either way,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say: Both this, a dry sponge with a handle, and that, one without a handle,

chunks.en: it may be moved on Shabbos,
chunks.st: may be moved on Shabbat

chunks.en: and it cannot become tamei.
chunks.st: and it does not become ritually impure.
chunks.stMore: A sponge is not among the substances that can become ritually impure, neither by Torah law nor by rabbinic decree.
